title: Guide exercise: abduction, blocking
description: A starter on a fresh problem: the loop of the library example abduction with every refinement replaced by a block. Find the interface, write a refinement, and compare with abduction. See the guide page "Your own loop: a walkthrough and a checklist".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Why does the car not start? A theory in clause form:
% pos(C,A): atom A occurs in clause C, neg(C,A): its negation does.
neg(1,flat).    pos(1,nostart).                   % a flat battery: no start
neg(2,flat).    pos(2,dim).                       % a flat battery: dim lights
neg(3,empty).   pos(3,nostart).                   % an empty tank: no start
neg(4,starter). pos(4,nostart).                   % a broken starter: no start
neg(5,plugs).   neg(5,damp). pos(5,nostart).      % fouled plugs in a damp engine: no start
neg(6,cold).    pos(6,flat). pos(6,damp).         % a cold night: flat battery or damp engine
neg(7,lights).  pos(7,flat).                      % lights left on: flat battery
neg(8,rain).    pos(8,damp).                      % rain: damp engine
pos(9,gauge).                                     % the fuel gauge shows fuel
neg(10,gauge).  neg(10,empty).                    % ... so the tank is not empty
% What may be assumed, and what has to be explained.
hypothesis(flat; empty; starter; plugs; cold; lights; rain).
manifestation(nostart).
clause(C) :- pos(C,_).
clause(C) :- neg(C,_).
atom(A) :- pos(_,A).
atom(A) :- neg(_,A).
fragments.description: The theory, the hypotheses and the manifestations. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k hypotheses ...
{ assume(H) : hypothesis(H) } k.
% ... that are consistent with the theory. The witness is a model w/1 of the theory in
% which the assumed hypotheses hold. It is not shown and not glued: Shape 2 blocks an
% accepted candidate by its interface atoms, so the witness does not multiply solutions.
{ w(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not w(A) : pos(C,A); w(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not w(H).
#show assume/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution, and the clause "always
% must change" ends the search.
{ always }.
:- not always.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): consistent sets of at most k hypotheses.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the assumed hypotheses.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a model of the theory and the assumed hypotheses in which some
% manifestation is false. Then the hypotheses do not entail the manifestations.
{ m(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not m(A) : pos(C,A); m(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not m(H).
:- m(A) : manifestation(A).
#show m/1.

% The model refutes every set of hypotheses that are all true in it. So a hypothesis
% that is false in the model has to be assumed.
relevant(assume(H)) :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
% If all hypotheses are true in the model, nothing explains the manifestations: blame
% the atom that is always true.
missing :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
relevant(always) :- not missing.
fragments.description: Looks for a model of theory and hypotheses in which a manifestation is false (solver C).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.block(M))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))
